headline: Pew Research Center finds that American women are more wary of AI than men, while men use chatbots somewhat more for work and information, and both use ChatGPT at the same rate.
score_reason: Pool score kept: solid survey, but the data are from February 2026 and the main study came out in June 2026, so only the gender breakdown is a new publication.
importance_line: Employers, product makers and policymakers get a clearer picture of who trusts and uses AI chatbots: women are more worried and men say chatbots help their productivity more, though these are self-reported answers from one US survey, not measured use.
summary: Pew Research Center reports from a survey of 5,119 US adults in February 2026 that women are about twice as likely to say AI will affect them personally for the worse over the next 20 years than for the better (33% against 17%), and 68% of women against 58% of men say AI is advancing too fast. Men are more likely to say chatbots help their productivity (35% against 25%) and to use Microsoft's Copilot (22% against 13%), but ChatGPT is used by identical shares of men and women; the figures come from a broader June 2026 Pew study, so the gender breakdown is the new part.
notes: Read in full on pewresearch.org (short read published 16 Oct 2026, an excerpt of a broader June 2026 study; survey fielded 17 to 23 Feb 2026). Kept as NEW because the gender analysis was published on 16 Oct; the underlying data are older, flagged in the summary and score reason.
